Help sustain Tasmania's volunteer emergency response capability.

 

 






 
The Team

Reporting to the Manager of Community Responders and Volunteers, you will have a statewide role in administrative responsibility for all Ambulance Tasmania volunteers and the GoodSAM community responder program.

You will engage with and support the three regional Volunteer and Responder Team Leaders.

The Role

Ambulance Tasmania is seeking a dedicated individual for the role of Volunteer and Community Responder Support Officer. This crucial position upholds service standards and provides essential support to our volunteer workforce and our GoodSAM community responder program. If you are passionate about championing and supporting volunteers, we encourage you to apply.

The Volunteer and Community Responder Support Officer provides specialised volunteer-focused administrative and operational coordination support to Ambulance Tasmania's volunteer and community responder capability.

The role supports the recruitment, onboarding, coordination, retention and sustainment of Volunteer Ambulance Officers (VAOs), GoodSAM Community Responders and the GoodSAM AED Registry.

Through effective administration and coordination support of these programs, the position contributes to the availability, readiness and sustainment of frontline volunteer and community responder resources, supporting Ambulance Tasmania's operational service delivery and community resilience.

The role operates under general direction within established policies, systems and procedures and is required to follow defined processes, apply sound administrative judgement within scope, and escalate complex or sensitive matters as appropriate while maintaining a high level of confidentiality.

Provide administrative support for the GoodSAM Community Responder program, including responder screening, onboarding, communications and routine coordination activities in accordance with established procedures.

Position: Aged or Disabled Carer
Type: Full-time
Employer: Exaudy Care Pty Ltd
Location: Narre Warren VIC 3805
Salary: $80,000 – $85,000 p.a.
About the Business
Exaudy Care Pty Ltd is a registered NDIS service provider based in Narre Warren, in Melbourne’s south-east, delivering personalised disability support services across the Melbourne metropolitan area and throughout Victoria. The company specialises in empowering participants through tailored support coordination, plan management, behaviour support, home and living assistance, community access, day programs, and clinical support. Guided by the EXAUDY values — Empathy, eXcellence, Accessibility, Understanding, Dedication, and You-focused — Exaudy Care is committed to “Empowering lives, delivering care from the heart.” The organisation fosters a compassionate, inclusive, and professional workplace culture where team members work collaboratively to uphold the highest standards of dignity, choice, and participant-centred care in line with NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission requirements.
About the Position
The Aged or Disabled Carer plays a vital role at Exaudy Care Pty Ltd, providing essential day-to-day support to aged and disabled clients to enhance their independence, quality of life, and overall wellbeing. Working within a supportive NDIS environment, the carer delivers practical assistance with personal care, household tasks, social activities, and emotional support while helping clients build confidence, social skills, and greater autonomy through individualised programs. This position is fundamental to delivering compassionate, person-centred care that respects participant choice and promotes dignity and inclusion.
Key Responsibilities
Providing general household assistance, including food preparation, housework, and keeping living areas clean.
Assisting with personal care, health and personal hygiene, dressing, and medication administration.
Offering emotional support, care, companionship, and friendship to promote wellbeing.
Supporting clients with physical mobility assistance and helping them perform important daily activities.
Undertaking tasks outside the home such as shopping and facilitating community access.
Ensuring a varied program of social and recreational activities to enrich client life.
Observing behaviour, maintaining accurate records of client progress, and assessing ongoing needs.
Assisting in developing and implementing client-specific programs to build social skills, self-image, self-confidence, and independence.
Requirements
Australian citizens and permanent residents are encouraged to apply.
Minimum AQF Certificate II or III in Individual Support, Community Services, or a related field, or at least one year of relevant experience.
Minimum of one year’s experience in a carer or support worker role within the disability or aged care sector.
Strong interpersonal skills, including empathy, patience, and the ability to build trusting relationships while promoting client dignity, choice, and independence.
Sound practical skills in personal care, household tasks, medication support, and accurate record-keeping.
Ability to work both independently and collaboratively within a team, with good organisational skills and attention to detail.
Current First Aid and CPR certification (preferred), valid driver’s licence with reliable transport (preferred), and willingness to obtain (or hold) a current NDIS Worker Screening Clearance.
How to Apply
To apply, applicants must submit their resume with a valid email address through this online portal. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

About the role

Join SA Pathology as a Domiciliary Support Officer and play an important role in coordinating domiciliary specimen collection services. Working both independently and as part of a supportive team, you will manage scheduling, maintain accurate records and provide administrative support to help ensure patients receive timely, high-quality care.

This is a varied role where you'll coordinate workloads, manage databases, communicate with patients and staff, and support the efficient day-to-day operation of the domiciliary phlebotomy service. Your organisation, attention to detail and commitment to customer service will help deliver a responsive and reliable service to the community.

About You

You are an organised and customer-focused professional who enjoys coordinating services and supporting both patients and colleagues.

- Communicate confidently with staff and patients

- Organise workloads and manage competing priorities

- Use Microsoft Office and databases confidently

- Deliver accurate administration and data entry

- Work independently and as part of a supportive team

About us

Statewide Clinical Support Services (SCSS) is a unique public healthcare organisation that serves health consumers and provides specialist clinical services to the health system in South Australia. SCSS encompasses BreastScreen SA, SA Dental, SA Medical Imaging, SA Pathology, and SA Pharmacy. Make a meaningful difference with UnitingCare Queensland 

At UnitingCare we are leaders in crisis response, the protection of vulnerable people and children, financial resilience and family wellbeing. Our FaDS (Family and Disability Services) team work passionately across Queensland to make a meaningful difference in people's lives.

As aSupported Living Facilitator, you'll be encouraged to grow, develop and feel empowered to make the everyday easier for the people we care so passionately about. Let's make a meaningful difference, together!

Your part in our UnitingCare team

You'll provide care to your clients living in the community, supporting their independence and improving their quality of life.

With no two days ever the same, you'll spend your time on the road completing your scheduled visits, interacting one-on-one with clients and their loved ones within their homes completing activities that include:

In home personal care, daily living assistance including showering, personal hygiene, meal preparation, house cleaning, laundry & ironing

Must be available to drive between clients with your own vehicle

Hours are mainly Monday to Friday between the hours of 9am-5pm

Providing care in accordance with their individualised Care Plan

Supporting with community based recreational and social activities

Transportation and assistance with shopping and appointments

Able to work effectively with others in a team-oriented environment and provide excellent support to clients and co-workers

Experience working in the Disability, Aged and Community sector is ideal but not essential -as long asyou have positive attitude and a willingness to learn

OpenDriversLicense and access to vehicle 

Car Insurance that is in your name

Flexible work arrangements to support work-life balance

Career development opportunities to challenge yourself, grow and make a meaningful difference 

A positive and inclusive team based on respect, shared standards, strong values and a commitment to serving others 

We'd love you to be part of our UnitingCare family

The second-largest Queensland employer, we're a proud not-for-profit with more than 16,500 staff and 9,000 volunteers across our brands of BlueCare, Lifeline, ARRCS, The Wesley Hospital, Buderim Private Hospital, St Stephen's Hospital, and St Andrew's War Memorial Hospital, and have been leading by example for more than 100 years.

Busy Bees is a leading global early learning provider, offering high-quality education in nurturing, purpose-built centres where educators are supported to grow, lead and make a real difference in children’s lives, with over 130 centres across Australia and around 3,000 employees.

Our Bee Safe Commitment: Child safety is at the heart of everything we do and is embedded in our people, places and processes. Help us give every child the Best Start in Life.

We’re seeking a passionate and experienced Lead Educator to join our team at Busy Bees at Chinchilla, located at 3 Braithwaite Street, Chinchilla QLD 4413, on a full-time basis. You will play a key role leading the daily learning program within your room, supporting educators, and creating a safe and engaging learning environment where children thrive. Sponsorship available for suitable applicants 482/494.

What you’ll do

Lead the planning and implementation of a high-quality educational program aligned with the EYLF
Inspire and mentor Educators within your room
Create a safe, inclusive and stimulating learning environment
Build strong, collaborative relationships with families and the local community
Ensure compliance with the National Quality Framework (NQF) and centre policies
Support children’s development, wellbeing, and learning outcomes through engaging play-based experiences

What you’ll bring

A genuine commitment to child safety, speaking up, always doing the right thing, and alignment with Busy Bees values
Diploma in Early Childhood Education and Care (or ACECQA-approved equivalent)
Current First Aid, CPR, Asthma and Anaphylaxis certification
Current Working with Children Check for QLD
Demonstrated experience leading a room within an early learning environment
Strong knowledge of the EYLF and National Quality Standards (NQS)
A collaborative and supportive leadership style

Why Busy Bees?

Because we offer the B.E.E.S. advantage:Better pay. Everyday balance. Education for growth. Support you can rely on.We live by our values of Care, Quality, Service, and Value to make a real impact on child safety and quality.

12.5% above-award pay, Retention Payments & everyday extras; uniform and laundry allowances included, so your take-home pay stays yours.
Family-friendly benefits; 50% childcare gap-fee discounts for permanent staff, because your family should benefit too.
Paid learning & development; First Aid, CPR & mandatory training covered, ongoing professional development, and access to our Busy Bees learning platform and ACCCO RTO pathways.
Supportive leaders & inclusive teams; hands-on leadership, strong tenure and a culture built on trust, respect and collaboration.
Career pathways that grow with you; opportunities & training to progress from Educator to leadership, management and area roles.
Wellbeing support that goes beyond work; free, confidential EAP access for you and your immediate family, when you need it most.

Employment is conditional on satisfactory, rigorous pre-employment checks (including WWCC, ID, Qualifications, Gecko Training, Work Rights, NQAITS register/Prohibited Persons & References) and child safety training, reflecting our strong commitment to safeguarding, equity, diversity and inclusion.

We are proud to be a child safe organisation, putting child safety at the heart of everything we do through our Bee Safe commitment.

Apply now to join Busy Bees at Chinchilla and take the next step in your leadership journey within a supportive and high-quality early learning environment.

Concrete Support Services (CSS) is a fully independent concrete testing and engineering consultancy supporting construction projects right across Melbourne. From our laboratory and field operations, we deliver concrete testing, materials assessment and technical advice that builders, contractors and engineers rely on to keep their projects moving and compliant. Because we operate as a completely independent laboratory, our clients know that every result we issue is backed by integrity, confidentiality and impartiality. Our work aligns with Australian Standards and NATA requirements, and our team combines decades of hands-on concrete technology expertise with a genuine commitment to service. What sets us apart is speed paired with accuracy we understand that critical site activities can’t wait, so we go out of our way to turn around reliable field and laboratory results promptly and to consistently exceed what our clients expect. As we continue to grow, we’re looking for a motivated Civil Engineering Technician to join our team at Oakleigh South and play a hands-on role in delivering the quality and responsiveness our clients count on.

Key Responsibilities
•	Carry out and coordinate a full program of on-site and in-laboratory tests on concrete, construction materials and soils including sampling fresh concrete, casting and curing specimens, slump and compressive strength testing all in accordance with Australian Standards.
•	Interpret job briefs, project specifications and work assignment instructions, then apply the appropriate testing procedures and select the correct equipment for each task.
•	Record, collate and analyse test results, perform the associated computations, and enter data accurately and promptly into our laboratory data-management systems so clients receive fast, dependable results.
•	Prepare technical sketches, charts, tabulations and test reports that support civil engineering works such as roads, drainage, water supply and sewerage reticulation systems, dams and structural elements where concrete and materials testing is required.
•	Conduct site inspections of concrete and civil works, and help organise and oversee sampling, re-testing and remedial or maintenance verification where required.
•	Estimate material quantities and associated costs, and check that materials and finished works comply with specifications, regulations and relevant contract provisions.
•	Collect field data during site surveys and sampling runs including on road, pavement and infrastructure projects and consolidate it for analysis and reporting.
•	Calibrate, maintain and correctly operate field and laboratory testing equipment, and keep clear records of its condition and use.
•	Uphold the laboratory’s quality management system and safeguard the integrity, impartiality and confidentiality of every result, in line with NATA and Australian Standards requirements.
•	Liaise professionally with clients, site supervisors and project engineers, providing clear technical support and rapid feedback to accommodate critical site timelines.
•	Support concrete mix design and quality-control activities, contributing observations and data that help clients meet their construction project needs.
•	Follow all workplace health and safety procedures and contribute to a safe, well-organised working environment both on site and in the laboratory.

About You
•	Strong attention to detail and a methodical, accurate approach to testing and record-keeping.
•	Reliable, punctual and able to manage priorities to meet time-critical site demands.
•	A team player who communicates clearly and professionally with colleagues and clients.
•	Committed to integrity, impartiality and confidentiality in all aspects of the work.
•	Safety-conscious, with a genuine respect for standards, procedures and compliance.
•	Physically capable of the practical, hands-on aspects of field and laboratory testing.
•	Willing to learn, take direction and grow within a supportive, quality-driven team.

Qualifications & Experience
•	An AQF Associate Degree, Advanced Diploma or Diploma in a relevant civil, engineering or materials-related discipline.
•	At least 1 year of relevant experience.

What We Offer
•	Salary:  $75,000 – $85,000 plus superannuation per annum.
•	Hours: Full-time position, typically 38 hours per week.
•	Location: Oakleigh South, VIC.

How to Apply
If this sounds like you, we’d love to hear from you. Please submit your resume together with a brief cover letter outlining your relevant experience and qualifications.

About the role

We are looking for an experienced Regional Support Manager who has worked in aged care, to join our team.

This key leadership role will be responsible for supporting the Regional Manager drive operational excellence across the portfolio of homes with a focus on quality, consistency and leadership development. The role will support Managers at the homes to optimise their workforce, continuously improve resident experience and ensure both clinical and non-clinical compliance.

We are looking for someone who has:

Experience in senior leadership roles in aged care.

A track record of leading large and diverse teams, with a proven ability to lead change and improvement in a complex environment.

Excellent communication, influencing and stakeholder engagement skills.

Outstanding customer service and a customer-first approach.

Strong commercial acumen.

Advanced knowledge and understanding of quantitative data and qualitative data, coupled with strong analytical and critical thinking skills.

Demonstrated experience in developing and implementing strategic operational plans, with a track record of driving compliance.

Knowledge and understanding of funding, health-aged care national policy and regulations.
